newsitem.title: INDIA: Chubb sees $2 bln insurance market in India.
newsitem.headline: Chubb sees $2 bln insurance market in India.

text.p: U.S.' insurance group Chubb Corporation expects to enter a $2 billion property and casualty insurance market in India once New Delhi opens up the sector, an Indian associate of Chubb said.

"They (Chubb) see the initial market for property and casualty insurance at $2 billion with an annual growth rate of 15 to 20 percent," Keya Sarkar, vice president of India's Kotak Mahindra Finance Ltd., told Reuters.

Chubb Corp signed a memorandum of understanding with Kotak Mahindra on Sunday to enter the Indian insurance market, currently under state control but expected to be opened up to private firms under an economic reform programme.

India has said it will set up an insurance regulatory authority, expected sometime next year, before opening up the business. A decision is expected by February 1997, when the next federal budget, officials say.
Sarkar said no financial details had been proposed for Chubb's planned venture. "We are waiting for the Indian government to come out with the guidelines," she said.
Sarkar said Chubb will concentrate on insurance linked to infrastructure, electrical industry and financial institutions and open a liaison office in India soon.
